reason: Re-opened packet.js tanakh 93 --verse 22.17: Rashi on ולא אבו says they expounded the limiting words of Joshua 1:18 (דרשו אכין ורקין), that one who rebels against the ruler's command might be liable even for a command to transgress, so Scripture says only (רק), i.e. a command to sin is excluded; applied by the guards to the king's order in this verse, which is what even a king's states. The key is the second sentence of 22:17, the exact lemma Rashi glosses. Plain sense states the order to kill in one plain clause (rule 6), faithful to 22:9 to 17. verse.js ok (1 Samuel 22:17, at [253,17]); entry-check ok, 42 words. Radak on the verse carries the same derash, so no conflict to name.
